chain.label: Certification concept relied solely on precluding ignition sources
chain.trigger: the design and certification concept that fuel tank explosions could be prevented solely by precluding all ignition sources

chain.label: 747 certificated with air conditioning packs beneath CWT and no means to limit heat transfer or render vapor nonflammable
chain.trigger: the design and certification of the Boeing 747 with heat sources located beneath the CWT with no means to reduce the heat transferred into the CWT or to render the fuel vapor in the tank nonflammable

caused_by.evidence: Contributing factors to the accident were the design and certification concept that fuel tank explosions could be prevented solely by precluding all ignition sources and the design and certification of the Boeing 747 with heat sources located beneath the CWT

chain.label: Aged, cracked FQIS wiring with breached insulation and silver-sulfide deposits, corouted with higher-voltage wires
chain.trigger: Almost every piece of recovered wire exhibited damage, including numerous cracks in the insulation (many of which penetrated to the core conductors)

caused_by.evidence: no special separation was required for other FQIS and fuel system wiring

chain.label: Air conditioning packs run about 2.5 hours on ground, heating CWT from below
chain.trigger: remained at gate 27 with the auxiliary power unit (APU) and two of its three air conditioning packs operating (for about 2 1/2 hours)

caused_by.evidence: the major heat load appears to be due to the high temperatures in the air conditioning equipment [bay]

chain.label: Nearly empty CWT holding only about 50 gallons of residual Jet A
chain.trigger: the accident airplane's CWT contained about 300 pounds of fuel; when the airplane was refueled at JFK, no additional fuel was added to the CWT

chain.label: Flammable fuel/air mixture present in CWT ullage at 13,800 feet
chain.trigger: an explosion of the center wing fuel tank (CWT), resulting from ignition of the flammable fuel/air mixture in the tank

caused_by.evidence: the highest ullage temperature measured within the CWT was 145 F... fuel/air mass ratios of 0.034, 0.046, and 0.054
fuel mass loading equivalent to 50 gallons in the CWT
heat sources located beneath the CWT with no means to reduce the heat transferred into the CWT or to render the fuel vapor in the tank nonflammable

chain.label: Short circuit outside CWT admits excessive voltage into FQIS wiring
chain.trigger: the most likely was a short circuit outside of the CWT that allowed excessive voltage to enter it through electrical wiring associated with the fuel quantity indication system

caused_by.evidence: evidence of arcing on generator cables routed with a wire bundle... two non-FQIS wires that would have been corouted in the same raceway with the CWT FQIS were found with possible arcing or heat damage
no special separation was required for other FQIS and fuel system wiring, including the fuel quantity probes and interconnecting wiring

chain.label: Ignition of the CWT fuel/air vapor
chain.trigger: The source of ignition energy for the explosion could not be determined with certainty

caused_by.evidence: allowed excessive voltage to enter it through electrical wiring associated with the fuel quantity indication system
ignition of the flammable fuel/air mixture in the tank

chain.label: CWT overpressure fractures SWB3, which rotates forward into the front spar
chain.trigger: An overpressure within the CWT initiated a failure at the top of SWB3... The top of SWB3 rotated forward and down and impacted the aft side of the front spar

caused_by.evidence: The National Transportation Safety Board determines that the probable cause of the TWA flight 800 accident was an explosion of the center wing fuel tank

chain.label: Belly structure and keel beam fail, forward fuselage separates
chain.trigger: Pieces of fuselage separated across the top of the airplane, thereby completely separating the forward fuselage from the remainder of the airplane

caused_by.evidence: Cracking on the right side of the front spar progressed downward, through the lower-pressure bulkhead and ring chord, and entered the fuselage

chain.label: Crippled aft airplane pitches up and climbs uncontrolled for about 34 seconds
chain.trigger: The main portion of the airplane (including the wings, most of the WCS, and the aft fuselage) continued in crippled flight for a period of time

caused_by.evidence: the airplane's c.g. would move aft from 21.1 to 57.8 percent MAC... an initial net nose-up pitching movement was indicated

chain.label: Fuel-fed fire on right wing and wing root during crippled flight
chain.trigger: the most intense fire effects were limited to the right wing, portions of the WCS, and a limited amount of fuselage structure above the right wing

caused_by.evidence: fire damage and soot deposit patterns on recovered wreckage indicated that some areas of fire existed on the main portion of the airplane as it continued in crippled flight

chain.label: Wing tips and wing center section fail; airplane breaks up in flight
chain.trigger: The wing tips separated at the outboard engines. The WCS separated adjacent to the left wing.

caused_by.evidence: at a high AOA and a 5.5 to 6 G load factor, the wing tips would fail... an additional 1 G increase in load factor would result in buckling (and ultimate failure) of the upper skin panel of the WCS
severe fire damage on many portions of the WCS... indicated that these areas remained attached to the right wing during the most intense fire

chain.label: Wreckage impacts the Atlantic Ocean near East Moriches
chain.trigger: crashed in the Atlantic Ocean near East Moriches, New York

caused_by.evidence: most of this portion of the fuselage struck the water as a large single piece

chain.label: All 230 occupants killed and airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: All 230 people on board were killed, and the airplane was destroyed.

caused_by.evidence: All injuries found in the victims were consistent with severe in-flight break up and subsequent water impact.
The airplane was destroyed by the explosion, breakup and impact forces, and fire.
